title: Azure Policy Guardrails That Enable Platform Teams
angle: Explain how an enterprise platform team can move from audit-only visibility to safe enforcement using initiatives, exemptions, remediation, policy as code, and measurable rollout gates.

title: Just-in-Time Azure Write Access for Development Teams with PIM
angle: Design a practical Azure access-governance pattern in which developers retain Reader access to the development resource group and activate an eligible Contributor role only for approved changes.
scenario: A development team has permanent Reader access at development resource-group scope. A developer who needs to deploy, modify, or delete a resource must activate an eligible Contributor assignment through Microsoft Entra PIM. Activation requires MFA, a change-ticket reference in the justification, and approval from a designated approver group aligned with reporting-manager responsibility. The organization configures an eight-hour maximum activation window, with users expected to request only the time needed. PIM audit history records eligibility, requests, approvals, activations, and expiry; Azure Activity Log records the resource write operations. The monitoring design correlates both records by identity and time.

steps: Contributor active for up to 8 hours

title: Passwordless Azure Deployments from GitHub Actions
angle: Give architects a practical design for GitHub Actions workload identity federation, least-privilege RBAC, environment protection, and migration away from client secrets.
scenario: Several application teams deploy Terraform and application releases into separate Azure development subscriptions. Existing pipelines use long-lived client secrets shared across repositories. The platform team must migrate each repository to GitHub OIDC, scope federated identities and Azure RBAC by environment, require protected-environment approval for production, and retain evidence that ties a workflow run to an Azure deployment.

title: AKS Network Isolation Without Breaking Delivery
angle: Describe the architecture decisions for a private AKS cluster, controlled egress, private endpoints, DNS, image pulls, and the operational trade-offs teams should test.
scenario: A platform team operates a private AKS cluster for multiple engineering teams. Workloads must pull images, retrieve secrets, send telemetry, and consume platform services without unrestricted internet egress. The design must preserve developer delivery speed while controlling DNS, private endpoints, firewall paths, and documented break-glass operations.

title: A Zero-Trust Operating Model for Azure Key Vault
angle: Build an operational blueprint covering RBAC, private connectivity, managed identities, rotation, logging, recovery controls, and separation of duties.

title: Designing an Azure Observability Baseline
angle: Show how to define a platform-level observability baseline using Azure Monitor, Log Analytics workspace design, diagnostic settings, alerts, and actionable service-level signals.

title: Bringing Defender for Cloud into the DevSecOps Loop
angle: Explain how security posture, code-to-cloud context, regulatory controls, and remediation ownership can become part of an engineering operating model rather than a dashboard-only exercise.
scenario: Application and platform teams deploy containerized workloads and infrastructure as code through GitHub. Security findings are visible in Defender for Cloud but lack engineering ownership and remediation targets. The DevSecOps design must connect repositories to cloud resources, route actionable findings to the owning team, block only high-confidence release risks, and retain evidence for governance reviews.

title: FinOps Guardrails for Enterprise Azure
angle: Present a practical operating model that connects hierarchy, tags, budgets, anomaly detection, reservations, and engineering accountability without inventing savings percentages.

title: Ransomware-Resilient Backup Architecture on Azure
angle: Explain how soft delete, immutability, authorization controls, monitoring, restore testing, and separation of duties fit together in a defensible backup architecture.

title: When Azure Container Apps Is the Right Platform Choice
angle: Compare the architectural concerns that make Container Apps suitable for APIs, event-driven services, and jobs, while clearly identifying when AKS or App Service is a better fit.

title: Turning an Azure Architecture Review into an Engineering Backlog
angle: Show how architects can use the Well-Architected Framework pillars to produce prioritized, owned, testable improvements instead of a static assessment document.
